notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($2,053,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts cash contributions from political committees (including union and business committees) and businesses to county commission, sheriff, clerk and recorder, treasurer, assessor and coroner candidates, reported to the Commissioner of Political Practices since 2023 (none were found). Montana bars corporations from giving to candidates directly, so most of this money comes through committees. Many contributions are dated the first day of their reporting period. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Montana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Fergus County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $4,172,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $734,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts cash contributions from political committees (including union and business committees) and businesses to candidates for mayor and city council, reported to the Commissioner of Political Practices since 2023 (none were found). City candidates are placed by the city of their mailing address, which can differ from the town they ran in. Montana bars corporations from giving to candidates directly, so most of this money comes through committees. Many contributions are dated the first day of their reporting period. Individuals, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 1 license-plate camera is mapped inside City of Lewistown's borders in OpenStreetMap (1 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Montana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 1 Flock Safety license-plate camera is mapped inside City of Lewistown's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
